description: 8 hospital EDs and 3 freestanding EDs: triage, medical screening, treatment, and EMS arrivals (about 1,530 visits and 310 ambulance arrivals a day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: EMTALA screening and stabilization duties continue during any outage (42 CFR 489.24(a)); diversion of ambulances not yet on hospital property is allowed only when the hospital lacks the staff or facilities to accept more emergency patients (489.24(b)); triage, allergy, and medication history unavailable; trauma center at H-01
manual_workaround: Business continuity access (BCA) downtime computers with reports refreshed every 15 minutes; paper ED records; phone and radio for EMS; regional diversion through the System Transfer and Command Center
dependent_third_parties: County EMS agencies; EHR vendor (support); carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: ED physicians and nurses; 11 dedicated emergency departments
quantified_impact_basis: ED professional and facility revenue lost to diversion and walk-outs (about 25% of visits) plus admissions lost through diversion, at the system average of $13.2 million revenue a day
h08_dependency: H-08 ED runs on SYS-13 until 2027-03-01
single_points_of_failure: Single EHR instance (DC-1 with DC-2 standby)

business_process: Inpatient care, nursing documentation, and medication administration
description: Care on about 1,600 occupied beds: orders, nursing documentation, barcode medication administration (BCMA), and handoffs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Medication administration records and active orders are needed within one medication pass (about 4 hours); wrong-patient and wrong-dose risk rises quickly on paper; record integrity duties (42 CFR 482.24(b))
manual_workaround: BCA medication administration and active order reports; paper MARs and order sheets; pharmacist double checks
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed discharges and admissions, overtime for paper workflows and back-entry, and lost inpatient revenue (about 40% of daily inpatient revenue at risk)
h08_dependency: H-08 inpatient units run on SYS-13

description: About 290 surgical and interventional cases a day: scheduling, pre-operative checks, anesthesia records, implant tracking
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cases in progress continue on paper anesthesia records; new elective cases stop without history, consents, and implant records; emergency surgery continues
manual_workaround: Paper anesthesia and nursing records; cancel or defer elective cases; emergency cases only
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-08; SYS-07 (operating room air handling)
dependent_third_parties: EHR vendor; implant and device vendors
quantified_impact_basis: About 60% of elective cases cancelled at an average of $9,400 per case plus idle staff cost
single_points_of_failure: Operating room air handling controlled by SYS-07 building automation

business_process: Laboratory testing and critical result reporting
description: 8 hospital laboratories (CLIA-certified): orders, specimen tracking, analyzer results, autoverification, critical value calls (about 21,000 results a day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Critical values must reach the responsible provider immediately (42 CFR 493.1291(g)); results must be accurately and reliably sent to the final report destination (493.1291(a)); specimen stability limits
manual_workaround: Analyzer printouts; manual result entry with second-person verification; phone critical values; send-out for stat work if a laboratory cannot report
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (laboratory module); analyzer middleware; integration engine; SYS-02
quantified_impact_basis: Repeat testing, send-out cost, overtime, and lost outpatient laboratory revenue
h08_dependency: H-08 laboratory orders arrive from SYS-13

description: Acquisition, storage, and reading of about 6,800 studies a day, including trauma and stroke CT
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Stroke and trauma CT reads are needed within minutes to hours; modalities can store studies locally for about 24 hours
manual_workaround: Read at modality consoles; route urgent studies by phone; divert CT-dependent ambulance traffic (stroke, major trauma) if a hospital has no CT reading path
dependent_people_or_facilities: Radiologists; technologists; 8 hospitals and 4 imaging centers
quantified_impact_basis: Lost outpatient imaging revenue and delayed inpatient discharges
h08_dependency: H-08 images reach SYS-08 over the site VPN
single_points_of_failure: PACS primary at DC-1 (replica at DC-2)

description: Pharmacist verification, automated dispensing cabinets (ADCs), IV compounding, and infusion pump drug libraries
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Medications must be verified and dispensed for every medication pass; ADCs and pump libraries must keep integrity
manual_workaround: ADC override with nurse double check; paper verification by pharmacists; pumps keep their last approved drug library
dependent_systems: SYS-01; ADC servers; pump drug-library servers; SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: ADC and pump vendors; drug wholesaler
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime, waste, and wholesaler expedite cost; safety impact dominates

business_process: Patient access, bed management, and transfer center
description: Registration, bed assignment, and the System Transfer and Command Center (about 260 inbound transfers a day), including EMS diversion coordination
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Patients cannot be registered or placed; transfer acceptance and diversion status must be tracked and shared with EMS and receiving hospitals (EMTALA transfer duties, 489.24(e))
manual_workaround: Paper registration and bed boards; transfer log on paper; EMS radio and analog lines
dependent_third_parties: County EMS agencies; regional healthcare coalitions
quantified_impact_basis: Lost transfers and rework; registration errors that later cause denials
single_points_of_failure: Transfer center at H-01 only (backup desk at H-02 never tested)

description: VoIP phones, secure clinical messaging, nurse call integration, overhead paging, and mass notification
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Rapid response, code teams, and critical result calls depend on phones and messaging; loss of communications removes the main downtime workaround
manual_workaround: Analog lines and EMS radio in every ED; runners; overhead paging on its own power; personal cell phones under the emergency communication plan (482.15(c)(3))
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and runner staffing; safety impact dominates
h08_dependency: H-08 phones on a separate legacy system
single_points_of_failure: Single VoIP call-control cluster per region

description: Building automation (including operating room and isolation room pressure), medical gas alarms, generator monitoring, nurse call, pneumatic tube
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Operating room and isolation room pressure, pharmacy and laboratory temperatures, and medical gas alarms protect patients; emergency power duties (482.15(e))
manual_workaround: Manual building operation by engineers on site; portable monitors; generator panels operated locally
dependent_third_parties: Building automation vendor; medical gas service contractor
quantified_impact_basis: Cancelled surgery in affected operating rooms and product loss in pharmacy and laboratory refrigeration
single_points_of_failure: OT not segmented at H-07 and H-08

description: Charge capture, claim submission, eligibility, and remittance posting; about 80% through the primary clearinghouse
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash, not time: payers accept late claims within filing limits, but each day of outage defers about $10.5 million of expected payments through the primary clearinghouse
manual_workaround: Queue claims; secondary clearinghouse (no contracted surge capacity); payer portals for the top 12 payers
quantified_impact_basis: Deferred collections: 80% of about $13.2 million of daily revenue flows through the primary clearinghouse
h08_dependency: H-08 claims through its own billing vendor

business_process: Patient billing, payment posting, and collections
description: Statements, patient payments, lockbox posting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Patient payments can queue; statement cycles can slip a week
manual_workaround: Hold statements; accept payments by phone through the bank virtual terminal
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed patient collections

description: 46 clinic locations of the employed physician group (about 5,200 visits a day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Clinic visits can be rescheduled for a day; refills and results follow-up create safety risk after 24 hours
manual_workaround: Printed schedules from BCA; paper visit notes; reschedule non-urgent visits
quantified_impact_basis: About 35% of visits deferred plus overtime for back-entry

business_process: Patient portal, telehealth, and FHIR API
description: Portal messaging, results, scheduling, and video visits for about 1.1 million active portal users; FHIR API for patient-authorized apps
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Patients can call instead; patient access to records and API duties apply but tolerate a short outage
manual_workaround: Contact center; phone visits; post outage notice on the public website
dependent_systems: Portal and API front end (SYS-04 Cloud A); SYS-01
quantified_impact_basis: Converted and lost video visits; contact center overtime

description: EHR access for about 70 independent physician practices (about 1,450 users) under hosting agreements and BAAs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Shares the ECIS, so its RTO equals the EHR RTO; hosting agreements commit 99.9% monthly availability and incident notice to practices
manual_workaround: Practices use their own downtime procedures and BCA reports pushed to them daily
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; Cloud A remote access gateway
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits and practice dissatisfaction; contract value about $31 million a year

description: 24x7 remote monitoring of about 210 ICU beds and telestroke consults for 14 partner hospitals, from the virtual care center at H-01
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Partner ICUs rely on remote intensivists overnight; telestroke decisions are time critical; contracts require notice to partner hospitals within 15 minutes of a service interruption
manual_workaround: Partner hospitals revert to local on-call coverage; telestroke by phone with image sharing through the partner PACS
dependent_third_parties: Tele-ICU software vendor; Cloud provider B; partner hospitals
dependent_people_or_facilities: Intensivists and critical care nurses in the virtual care center
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits; patient safety at partner hospitals dominates
single_points_of_failure: Virtual care center at H-01 (no alternate site)

description: Biweekly payroll for 12,000 employees (about $34 million a run); SOX-relevant
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll cutoff 72 hours before pay date; wage payment laws and workforce retention
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll with adjustments through the payroll provider
quantified_impact_basis: Penalties, manual adjustments, and retention risk

description: Ordering and stocking supplies, implants, and pharmaceuticals for 8 hospitals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Hospitals hold about 3 days of most supplies; implants and blood products need tracking
manual_workaround: Manual orders by phone and email to top distributors; paper implant logs
quantified_impact_basis: Expedite fees and product substitutions

description: Quarterly and annual close, SOX controls, Form 10-Q and 10-K preparation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines; the MTD drops to 48 hours in the quarter-end close window; SOX IT general controls
manual_workaround: Extend the close calendar; manual journal entries with dual approval
dependent_systems: SYS-09; data and analytics platform (Cloud B)
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and outside advisor cost; missed filing would be Severe

business_process: Health information management, release of information, and public health reporting
description: Record requests, coding, HIE exchange, and electronic laboratory, case, immunization, and syndromic reporting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Reportable results and case reports have state deadlines; patient access requests have regulatory response times
manual_workaround: Fax or phone reports to the health department; queue requests
dependent_third_parties: Health information exchanges; state health departments
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and coding backlog
h08_dependency: H-08 reports through its own vendor

business_process: H-08 clinical operations on the legacy EHR
description: All clinical care at H-08 (100 beds and its ED) until the 2027-03-01 migration
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same safety drivers as BP-01 and BP-02; the legacy vendor contract states a 24-hour RTO and the vendor backs up every 4 hours (actual RPO 4 hours)
manual_workaround: Paper downtime; transfer high-acuity patients to H-06 or H-07
dependent_systems: SYS-13; legacy directory; site VPN to the integration engine
quantified_impact_basis: About 7% of system inpatient and ED revenue

description: 24-bed inpatient behavioral health unit and addiction medicine service at H-03
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Part 2 records need segmented access and the 2.16 safeguards in downtime as well as normal operation; patients need continuous care
manual_workaround: Paper records kept in the locked unit office; consent forms checked before any disclosure
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and delayed admissions
